newsitem.title: USA: Apple to change clone licensing deals.
newsitem.headline: Apple to change clone licensing deals.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc in a few weeks will change its royalty agreements with computer makers that license its Macintosh operating system software, the company said Wednesday.
The move would increase Apple's revenue for the next few months but would hamper the health of Macintosh hardware and software in the long run, analysts said.
A handful of computer companies, such as Umax Technologies Inc and Power Computing Corp, make computers that are based on Apple's Macintosh software. They pay Apple a licensing fee for the right.

These so-called Mac clone makers have thrived in recent months because they sell computers that cost less than comparable offerings from Apple. Their success has come partly at a cost to Apple, which continues to see unit shipments of its Macs fall.
Apple is reviewing its licensing agreements with the clone companies, said Natalie Welch, an Apple spokeswoman.
She would not say whether the company would raise the fees, but analysts said Apple likely will raise them to increase revenues.

"The short-term solution to raising revenue is to raise the royalties," said Matt Sargent, an analyst at market researcher Computer Intelligence InfoCorp in San Diego. "That would be a mistake. It would not only kill the Macintosh operating system but kill Apple itself."

The only good news about Apple in recent weeks has been that the Macintosh operating system's share of the market has increased because of the success of the clone makers, Sargent said. By raising its licensing fees, Apple would hamper the growth of the clone makers and discourage software companies from developing products for the Macintosh, he said.
